report.title: Package quality/conformance score computable with zero telemetry and zero network
report.question_or_target: Which npm, OpenSSF Scorecard, and Packagist signals are computable from package bytes alone, and how does the byte-only npm subset rank-correlate with the full online score on 30 real packages?

answer.npm: Package bytes support an adapted manifest/documentation/test-presence/branding conformance metric. It is not an exact npms subset because registry deprecation conditions carefulness, upstream badge collection is not reconstructed exactly, and official component scores use cross-package calibration; downloads, maintenance, CI/coverage, freshness, and vulnerability status remain external.
answer.openssf_scorecard: Nine checks are statically executable from local bytes, but seven are only observable if repository configs/workflows were shipped. Fuzzing is hybrid; Vulnerabilities and repository/service-state checks are not byte-only.
answer.packagist: packagist.org currently exposes query ranking, popularity telemetry, abandonment state, downloads, and favers, not a scalar quality rating. Composer manifest conformance is byte-computable but is not the current ranking formula.

measured_correlation.offline_metric_label: npms-derived byte-only conformance metric; not the exact online npms quality score
measured_correlation.interpretation: The adapted metric is associated with the online quality dimension on this cohort, but it has no demonstrated association with the full online score (rho=0.111086400553; permutation p=0.555944405559).

answer.recommended_marketplace_use: Treat the offline score as a recomputable conformance/evidence-coverage score with explicit NOT-OBSERVABLE states; do not present it as reputation, popularity, vulnerability status, or a surrogate for the full online score.
